note: Gabriel phthalimide synthesis, drawn as THREE arrows across two rows, compressed here into the one overall reaction the schema allows. Drawn: phthalimide --KOH--> potassium phthalimide --R-X--> N-alkylphthalimide (row 1, labelled 'Phthalimide' and 'N-Alkylphthalimide'); then N-alkylphthalimide --NaOH(aq)--> disodium phthalate + R-NH2, the amine labelled '(1 degree amine)' (row 2). The two drawn intermediates are lost from the SMILES field and are recorded here instead: potassium phthalimide is O=C1[N-]C(=O)c2ccccc21.[K+] (the book draws the nitrogen with a minus sign and K+ beside it, an ion pair, not an N-K bond) and N-alkylphthalimide is O=C1N([*])C(=O)c2ccccc21. Everything written over an arrow is an agent: KOH, R-X and NaOH(aq). R is a letter with no structure attached, so it is a wildcard; X is likewise only a letter, so the alkyl halide is written as two bonded wildcards [*][*] rather than guessing a halogen. The imide rings are drawn with the two C=O and the N explicit; the benzo ring is a plain Kekule hexagon. Product carboxylates are drawn as O-Na+ with the charge shown, so they are written as separated ions. No wedge or dash anywhere, so no stereochemistry. Confidence is probable only because of the three-arrow compression and the wildcard alkyl halide.
